name: Hive Circuit • Cell kit
description: Presentation deck — how a colony ships work; hexagons are atmosphere.

slides.title: A colony that still feels human
items: Roles, routes, and the cells that carry the week

slides.title: How the hive moves
items: Same cell shape so handoffs never reinvent the box.
Work travels the warmest path, not the longest memo.
New work starts next to veterans, not in a side channel.

slides.title: Cells on the floor
items: Owns intake. Turns noise into a ticket the floor can run.
Protects focus. Blocks scope that would crack the comb.
Brings proof back. Closes the loop in the same cell.

slides.title: Queen cell
items: Sets the week’s direction — one sentence, no slide deck.
Forty people, one cadence. Standups stay under eight minutes.
Specialists that plug in, then leave the comb intact.
Shared docs and templates. No private honey pots.

slides.title: The shell holds
items: Six clear walls beat four soft ones when pressure hits.

slides.title: Follow the warmth
items: If a cell goes cold, move the work before you add process.

slides.title: WAX
items: A hive is a city that still fits in a hand.

slides.title: Pack tight. Leave room to breathe.
